dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Pense: quantas vezes o número 5 cabe dentro do 6? O que sobra dessa divisão?
Tente separar o 6/5 em (5/5) + (1/5). Quanto vale 5/5? Esse valor será sua parte inteira.
Você tem 1 inteiro (que são 5 pedaços) e ainda sobra 1 pedaço. Como você escreveria isso na forma de número misto?
Quase lá! Coloque '1' na parte inteira (m1) e a fração que sobrou (1/5) nos campos m2 e m3.
Onde fica o número 1 na reta? Como a fração é maior que 1, o ponto deve estar à direita ou à esquerda do 1?
Localize o 1 na reta. Como o denominador é 5, cada espaço entre os números inteiros foi dividido em 5 partes. Conte uma dessas partes após o 1.
O ponto deve ficar exatamente na primeira marca após o número 1.
Coloque o ponto na primeira subdivisão depois do número 1 na reta numérica.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 5 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)
grupo com m1/m2/m3, exibido depois de Convert
botão "Convert": abre as caixas do número misto (m1, m2, m3) para reescrever a fração
campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico: parte inteira do número misto

passos.acao: In field f1, enter the numerator: the number of gum pieces Brandon gave Luke.
In field f2, enter the denominator: the number of pieces in one pack.
Use the fraction fields to represent the amount Brandon gave as a fraction greater than one.
Click Convert to rewrite 6/5 as a mixed number in the rightFraction group.
On the number line from 0 to 2, mark the point for 6/5.
Click Done after entering the fraction and marking its position.

erros.devolutiva: You used the pack size for the numerator. The numerator represents the pieces Brandon gave, while the denominator represents the pieces in each pack.

erros.devolutiva: You used two complete packs, but only one complete group of five fits into six. The quotient must count complete groups of five.
The denominator stays the same because the size of each part has not changed. Keep five as the denominator of the remaining fraction.

dicas.texto: Focus on the amount Brandon gave away, not on the size of each pack.
For a fraction, place the counted amount in the top field.
Use the number of individual gum pieces mentioned in the story.
Enter the number of pieces Brandon gave Luke in f1.
Think about what one whole pack contains.
For a fraction, place the size of one equal group in the bottom field.
Read the sentence that describes how many pieces are in each pack.
Enter the number of gum pieces contained in one pack in f2.
Compare the number of pieces given with the number of pieces in one whole pack.
Keep the amount given as the numerator and the pack size as the denominator.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator is larger than its denominator.
Represent the given pieces over the pieces in one pack, then check that the top number is larger than the bottom number.
A mixed number shows complete wholes first and the remaining fractional part second.
Divide the numerator by the denominator; use the quotient for the whole number and the remainder for the new numerator.
Find how many complete groups of five fit into six, then identify how many pieces remain.
Enter the whole-number quotient in m1, the remainder in m2, and keep the original denominator in m3.
Locate the point by relating the improper fraction to one whole and its remaining part.
Divide the interval from 0 to 2 into fifths and count from zero.
First find 1 on the line, then move one fifth farther to the right.
Place the point at the first fifth-mark after 1, using the hidden fifth-part spacing.
Review whether your fraction and number-line point describe the same amount.
Check the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and marked position before finishing.
Make sure the point is one fifth to the right of 1 and that the mixed-number group is complete.
When every field and the number-line point agree, press the Done button.

exercicio.statement:
Brandon had packs of gum that he shared with his friend. Each pack had five pieces. He gave Luke six pieces. Describe the number of packs of gum Brandon gave away and show the value on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you.
